steps.body: Lining up the decimal points lines up every place at once: tenths above tenths, hundredths above hundredths.
steps.narration: Lining up the decimal points lines up every place at once: tenths above tenths, hundredths above hundredths.

widget.prompt: Work 3.47 + 2.85 in columns. Tap each column to add it.

commonResults.feedback: 622 hundredths stranded the carry out of the hundredths column — ten hundredths make a tenth and must move left.
Two carries went missing; each stranded carry costs exactly the bundle it was carrying.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add column by column from the ones; when a column reaches 10 or more, trade and carry.
widget.successFeedback: 24,681 + 13,247 = 37,928 — the ones make 8 with a carry that the tens must include.

predict.prompt: Adding 3.4 + 2.25, which digits belong in the same column?
predict.reveal: The point marks where the whole numbers end, so aligning it puts tenths over tenths automatically.

cml.actionGoal: Work in the smallest place the numbers use, then decide where the point belongs for g5dc align.
invariants: A decimal is place value continued past the ones: computing in the smallest shared place turns g5dc align into whole-number arithmetic, and the point's position records which place the digits landed in.
misconceptions: Right-aligning digits instead of the points, treating a trailing zero as a change in value, or losing count of the decimal places a product carries.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the point moved one place left, how many times smaller would the amount become?

widget.prompt: Adding 3.4 + 2.25, why line up the decimal points rather than the right-hand digits?

options.label: Matching place values line up
options.feedback: Correct — the point marks where the whole numbers end, so aligning it aligns every place at once.

options.label: Because the longer number always goes on top
options.feedback: Which number is longer has nothing to do with it; place value is what must match.

options.label: Because 3.4 has fewer digits
options.feedback: Digit count is not the issue — 3.4 and 3.40 are the same amount but look different lengths.

options.label: It does not matter — either way works
options.feedback: Right-aligning would add the 4 tenths to the 5 hundredths, which combines different-sized pieces.
